name: Karunakara Perumal Shrine (Thirukkaragam), Kanchipuram
deity: Vishnu as Karunakara Perumal, with the Goddess Padmamani Nachiyar — the Divya Desam of Thirukkaragam, housed within the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple
period: A Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
dynasty: Pallava (host temple, with Chola, Vijayanagara and Nayak additions)
summary: Thirukkaragam is one of four Divya Desams within the Ulagalantha Perumal complex in Kanchipuram, where Vishnu is worshipped as Karunakara, the merciful Lord, in the third precinct, sung by Thirumangai Alvar.

sections.history: Thirukkaragam is not a temple apart but a Divya Desam within the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple of Periya Kanchi, the same complex that holds Thiruooragam, Thiruneeragam and Thirukkarvanam. The four are believed to have once been independent shrines, and a single verse of Thirumangai Alvar names them together; Thirumangai Alvar is the Alvar who sang this shrine in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. The host temple is believed to be a Pallava foundation, with later additions by the Medieval Cholas, the Vijayanagara kings and the Nayaks, and is administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department. As one of the 108 Divya Desams, Thirukkaragam belongs to Thondai Nadu, the Tamil country around Kanchipuram.
sections.architecture: The shrine stands in the third precinct, or prakaram, of the Ulagalantha Perumal complex, beyond the main sanctum of Trivikrama. Karunakara Perumal is worshipped seated on Adisesha, with Padmamani Nachiyar, also called Ramamani Thayar, as his consort. The sanctum rises under the Vamana Vimanam, and its sacred water is the Agraya Theertham. The setting is a small, quiet sanctum within the larger walled complex.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the sage Garga, who performed penance at this place and obtained knowledge; the spot was called Garagaham after him, and in time Kaaragam, from which the name Thirukkaragam is held to come. The Lord who appeared to the sage is honoured here as Karunakara, the compassionate one, whose mercy answers the patient devotion of the sage and of every pilgrim who follows him.
sections.festivals: The shrine keeps the calendar of the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple: Vaikunta Ekadashi, the annual Brahmotsavam with processions through the streets of Kanchipuram, and the recitation of the Divya Prabandham in the month of Margazhi. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thirukkaragam rewards the pilgrim who goes beyond the great sanctum of Trivikrama and walks on to the third precinct. Look for the seated Karunakara Perumal with Padmamani Nachiyar, and ask the priests about the Agraya Theertham and the legend of the sage Garga. Visit it with the other three Divya Desams of the complex to complete a single, unhurried circuit.

visit.timings: The shrine opens with the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple: morning and evening darshan sessions with a midday closure. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctums; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: This is a shrine inside the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple in the old town of Kanchipuram (Periya Kanchi); enter by that temple's gateway and ask for Thirukkaragam in the third precinct. Chennai, about 70 km to the north-east, is the nearest major airport, and Kanchipuram town is the nearest railhead.
